title: Typing von Willebrand Disease: Level, Ratio, Then the Special Tests
summary: Use VWF antigen, platelet-binding activity and factor VIII levels and ratios to classify von Willebrand disease, then confirm with multimers, low-dose ristocetin and factor VIII binding — and know why desmopressin can harm type 2B.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 37 Hit 2 (VWD most common), Hit 3 (functional ratios), Hit 6 (type 2B), Hit 9 (platelet-type VWD), Hit 10 (type 2N), Hit 11 (type 3), Hit 16 (PFA-100 workup) and Traps 2–3. Checked against Tosetto & Eikenboom 2026 (summarizing the ASH ISTH NHF WFH 2021 guideline), James 2021 (abstract), Flood & Haberichter 2026 and Seidizadeh 2025. The reviewer uses a 0.6 ratio cut-off for type 2 and for 2N; the guideline suggests < 0.7 (register flag rv-vwd-ratio). Not taught: “type 1 ≈ 75% of cases” and “type 3 FVIII typically < 10%” (not in the sources read), and LD-RIPA ristocetin concentrations.

objectives: Explain the two functions of VWF and the three first-level tests.
Classify VWD by VWF level and by activity/antigen and FVIII/antigen ratios.
Choose multimer analysis, low-dose RIPA and VWF:FVIIIB to subtype type 2 VWD.
Explain why desmopressin may be contraindicated in type 2B VWD.

scenes.title: Heavy bleeding, normal platelet count
scenes.altText: A patient card: 19-year-old with heavy menstrual bleeding and nosebleeds since childhood; mother bleeds after dental work. Result tokens: platelet count normal; PT normal; aPTT normal; PFA-100 closure time prolonged on both cartridges, no antiplatelet drugs. A question token: “Which von Willebrand type — or none?” The cartoon scientist frowns.

cues.text: A 19-year-old has heavy periods and nosebleeds since childhood. Her mother bleeds after dental work.
Platelet count, PT and aPTT are normal. But the PFA-100 closure time is prolonged on both cartridges, and she takes no antiplatelet drugs.
That points to von Willebrand disease, the most common inherited bleeding disorder. But which type? The answer changes treatment.

props.label: Which von Willebrand type — or none?

scenes.title: VWF has two jobs — and three first-level tests
scenes.altText: A VWF token (a long multimer string) shows two jobs: on the left it bridges exposed collagen to platelet GPIb; on the right it carries factor VIII, protecting it. Three test cards appear: VWF:Ag (how much VWF), VWF platelet-binding activity (VWF:RCo or a GPIb-based assay — how well it grabs platelets), and FVIII:C (how much factor VIII it is carrying). A note: aPTT is prolonged only if FVIII is low; a normal aPTT does not rule out VWD.

cues.text: Von Willebrand factor has two jobs. It bridges exposed collagen to platelets through the GPIb receptor.
And it carries factor VIII in plasma, protecting it from rapid clearance.
So the first-level tests measure three things: how much VWF there is, the VWF antigen; how well it binds platelets, the activity assay; and factor VIII.
The activity assay is the ristocetin cofactor test or a newer GPIb-based assay.
The aPTT only lengthens when factor VIII is low, so a normal aPTT does not rule out VWD.

props.label: Normal aPTT does not rule out VWD

scenes.title: Sorting by numbers: level, then ratio
scenes.altText: A decision ladder builds. Step 1, level: VWF:Ag or activity < 30 IU/dL → VWD regardless of bleeding; 30–50 IU/dL → type 1 only with abnormal bleeding (otherwise “low VWF”); ≥ 50 usually normal. Step 2, ratios: activity/Ag < 0.7 → type 2 (2A, 2B or 2M); FVIII/Ag < 0.7 → type 2N or mild hemophilia A. Step 3: VWF:Ag virtually undetectable → type 3. A ratio meter slides from 1.0 down to 0.45 and the type 2 bin lights.

cues.text: Step one is the level. If VWF antigen or activity is below 30 IU per deciliter, it is VWD, whatever the bleeding history.
Between 30 and 50, call it type 1 only if the bleeding is abnormal; otherwise it is low VWF. Repeat abnormal results, because stress, inflammation and pregnancy raise VWF.
Step two is the ratio. If activity divided by antigen is below 0.7, the VWF is there but works poorly: type 2A, 2B or 2M.
If factor VIII divided by VWF antigen is below 0.7, think type 2N, or mild hemophilia A.
And if VWF antigen is virtually undetectable, it is type 3, the severe form with almost no VWF at all.

scenes.title: Second-level tests: multimers, low-dose RIPA, FVIII binding
scenes.altText: Three cards. Multimers: high-molecular-weight multimers missing in 2A and 2B, full range present in 2M (collagen-binding/Ag ratio can substitute). Low-dose RIPA: agglutination at low ristocetin concentrations = 2B — or platelet-type VWD (a GP1BA gain-of-function); separate them with a RIPA mixing study or VWF/GP1BA genetic testing. VWF:FVIIIB binding assay: reduced in 2N, normal in hemophilia A. A treatment card: desmopressin works for most type 1 but may cause severe thrombocytopenia in 2B; VWF concentrate is preferred in 2B and 2N. Back to the patient: activity/Ag 0.45, HMW multimers missing, low-dose RIPA not enhanced → type 2A.

cues.text: For a low activity-to-antigen ratio, run multimers. Large multimers are missing in types 2A and 2B but present in 2M.
Low-dose ristocetin separates 2B. Its VWF grabs GPIb too eagerly, so platelets agglutinate at ristocetin doses that do nothing to normal plasma.
Platelet-type VWD gives the same result, but the defect is in the platelet receptor. A RIPA mixing study or gene testing tells them apart.
For a low factor VIII ratio, the VWF–factor VIII binding assay decides: reduced in 2N, normal in hemophilia A.
Our patient has a ratio of 0.45, missing large multimers and no low-dose response: type 2A. Desmopressin may not help type 2, and in 2B it can drop the platelets.

props.title: Treatment hinges on type
lines: 2B: DDAVP may crash platelets → VWF concentrate

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards appear in turn: “Type 2 means an activity/Ag ratio < 0.6” (✓ the 2021 guideline suggests < 0.7, with low certainty); “Low FVIII with normal VWF = hemophilia A” (✓ could be type 2N — run VWF:FVIIIB); “Give DDAVP to every VWD patient” (✓ it may cause severe thrombocytopenia in 2B; use VWF concentrate).

cues.text: Trap one: type 2 means a ratio below 0.6. The 2021 international guideline suggests below 0.7, though the certainty is low.
Trap two: low factor VIII with normal VWF is hemophilia A. It could be type 2N. Run the factor VIII binding assay.
Trap three: give desmopressin to every VWD patient. Not in 2B, where it can cause severe thrombocytopenia; VWF concentrate is preferred.

scenes.title: Low, lame, lost — 2B grabs, 2N drops
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Low, lame, lost.” Type 1 = low amount; type 2 = lame function; type 3 = lost entirely. Plus: “2B grabs too hard; 2N drops its passenger (FVIII).” A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: low, lame, lost. Type 1 has a low amount, type 2 works lamely, type 3 is lost. And 2B grabs platelets too hard, while 2N drops its passenger, factor VIII.
Where it breaks: ratio cut-offs vary between labs and assays; 2M has normal multimers but poor binding; platelet-type VWD mimics 2B; and a normal PFA-100 does not exclude mild VWD.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Level: < 30 IU/dL = VWD · 30–50 = type 1 only with bleeding · ratio < 0.7 = type 2 · undetectable = type 3”, “Second level: multimers, low-dose RIPA (2B vs platelet-type), VWF:FVIIIB (2N vs hemophilia A) · no DDAVP in 2B”.

cues.text: Type VWD by level first, then by the activity-to-antigen and factor VIII-to-antigen ratios, then confirm with multimers, low-dose ristocetin and factor VIII binding — because desmopressin can harm type 2B.

props.label: < 30 IU/dL = VWD · 30–50 + bleeding = type 1 · ratio < 0.7 = type 2 · no VWF = type 3
Multimers · low-dose RIPA (2B vs PT-VWD) · VWF:FVIIIB (2N vs hemophilia A) · no DDAVP in 2B

explanation.what: Plain language: VWF glues platelets to damaged vessel walls and carries factor VIII; VWD is too little VWF (type 1), VWF that works badly (type 2) or almost none (type 3). Scientific terms: VWF:Ag, VWF platelet-binding activity (VWF:RCo, GPIb-based assays), FVIII:C, multimers, ristocetin-induced platelet agglutination (RIPA), VWF:FVIIIB, platelet-type VWD (GP1BA gain-of-function).
explanation.why: Activity disproportionately lower than antigen means dysfunctional VWF (type 2). In 2A and 2B, high-molecular-weight multimers are lost; in 2M, multimers are normal but A1-domain binding to GPIb is reduced. In 2B, VWF binds GPIb with increased affinity, so low-dose ristocetin agglutinates platelets and platelets are cleared (thrombocytopenia). In 2N, VWF cannot bind FVIII, so FVIII falls.
explanation.measure: VWF:Ag and/or activity < 30 IU/dL → VWD regardless of bleeding; 30–50 IU/dL → type 1 only with abnormal bleeding; ≥ 50 IU/dL usually normal; repeat because VWF rises with acute phase, inflammation and pregnancy. Activity/Ag < 0.7 → 2A/2B/2M; FVIII/Ag < 0.7 → 2N or mild hemophilia A. Undetectable VWF:Ag → type 3.
explanation.differs: 2A vs 2M: multimers (or VWF:CB/Ag). 2B vs platelet-type VWD: RIPA mixing study or VWF/GP1BA genetics. 2N vs mild hemophilia A: VWF:FVIIIB (reduced in 2N).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: a ratio below the type 2 cut-off, low-dose RIPA in 2B, DDAVP contraindication in 2B, 2N vs hemophilia A, and normal aPTT not excluding VWD.

comparisons.title: Type 2B VWD vs platelet-type VWD
comparisons.distinguisher: RIPA mixing study or VWF/GP1BA genetic testing.

comparisons.title: Type 2N VWD vs mild hemophilia A

mnemonic.explanation: Type 1 = low amount, type 2 = lame function, type 3 = lost; 2B VWF grabs GPIb too hard, 2N VWF drops its FVIII passenger.
mnemonic.limitation: Ratio cut-offs vary by lab and assay; 2M has normal multimers but poor binding; platelet-type VWD mimics 2B; a normal PFA-100 does not exclude mild VWD.

takeaway: Type VWD by level first, then by the activity-to-antigen and factor VIII-to-antigen ratios, then confirm with multimers, low-dose ristocetin and factor VIII binding — because desmopressin can harm type 2B.

questions.stem: VWF:Ag 42 IU/dL, VWF platelet-binding activity 17 IU/dL, FVIII 48 IU/dL. Multimers show loss of high-molecular-weight forms, and low-dose ristocetin causes no agglutination. Which type is most likely?

options.rationale: Correct. Activity/Ag = 0.40 (< 0.7) with missing HMW multimers and no low-dose RIPA response fits 2A.
Incorrect. 2B also loses HMW multimers but shows enhanced agglutination at low-dose ristocetin.
Incorrect. 2M has a low ratio but a normal multimer pattern.
Incorrect. In type 1, activity falls in proportion to antigen (ratio ≥ 0.7).

questions.stem: A woman has FVIII 14 IU/dL with VWF:Ag 85 IU/dL and normal VWF activity. Her brother and father are similarly affected. Which test best distinguishes the likely causes?

options.rationale: Correct. FVIII/Ag < 0.7 suggests type 2N or mild hemophilia A; VWF:FVIIIB is reduced in 2N and normal in hemophilia A.
Incorrect. Low-dose RIPA identifies 2B or platelet-type VWD.
Incorrect. Multimers separate 2A/2B from 2M; they are normal in 2N.
Incorrect. This tests platelet receptors, not VWF–FVIII binding.

questions.stem: A patient with mild thrombocytopenia shows platelet agglutination at a low ristocetin concentration that does not agglutinate normal platelet-rich plasma. What is the best next step?

options.text: RIPA mixing study or VWF/GP1BA genetic testing
options.rationale: Correct. Both type 2B and platelet-type VWD over-respond to low-dose ristocetin; mixing or genetics locates the defect.
Incorrect. Enhanced low-dose RIPA points to 2B or platelet-type VWD, which are often misdiagnosed as ITP.
Incorrect. Desmopressin may cause severe thrombocytopenia in 2B.
Incorrect. Type 1 does not show enhanced low-dose ristocetin agglutination.

references.usedFor: PT-VWD: autosomal dominant GP1BA gain-of-function; excessive GPIbα–VWF binding, loss of HMW multimers and thrombocytopenia; enhanced RIPA; without RIPA mixing study or VWF/GP1BA genetic testing often misdiagnosed as 2B or ITP; 2B more common.

claims.text: VWF carries FVIII and binds GPIb; first-level tests VWF:Ag, platelet-binding activity, FVIII:C; normal aPTT and normal PFA-100 do not exclude VWD.
< 30 IU/dL → VWD; 30–50 → type 1 only with abnormal bleeding; repeat testing; activity/Ag < 0.7 → type 2 (low certainty); FVIII/Ag < 0.7 → 2N or mild hemophilia A; undetectable Ag → type 3.
Multimers (HMW missing in 2A/2B, full in 2M); low-dose RIPA enhanced in 2B and PT-VWD; mixing study or genetics separates them; VWF:FVIIIB reduced in 2N, normal in hemophilia A.
DDAVP for most type 1; may induce severe thrombocytopenia in 2B; VWF concentrate preferred in 2B and 2N.
Type 1 accounts for ~75% of VWD; type 3 FVIII typically < 10%; LD-RIPA at 0.3–0.5 mg/mL.
